To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of bilingual children on narrative assessment tasks in L2 and L1 may not be comparable.

(a) children’s narrative skills are related to their language proficiencies; (b) children’s narrative performance in the second language (English) is related to their narrative skills in Spanish; (c) children’s narrative recall is related to their language proficiency; and (d) children’s narrative production is related to their oral language skills.

(1) bilingual children exhibit different levels of narrative competence in their two languages, and (2) narrative assessment in L1 and in L2 may not pose the same processing demands on bilingual children.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the narrative performance of bilingual children in two languages, and its relationship to literacy development.
the narrative skills of typically developing bilingual children and their implications for reading and writing development.
the development of narrative skills and the implications for literacy development of bilingual Spanish-English-speaking children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bilingual child is a child with a bilingual profile, which is not a simple combination of two monolingual profiles.
the narrative skills of the bilingual children are comparable to those of the monolingual children, but not identical.
bilingualism is a complex phenomenon, and the narrative performance of bilinguals should be assessed in both languages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the assessment of bilingual children should include both languages, but the assessment tasks should also be tailored to each child’s bilingual profile.
narrative skills are important in both languages for bilingual children.
the bilingualism continuum should be taken into account when assessing the narrative skills of bilingual children.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bilinguals are a heterogeneous group.
narrative performance should be examined in the context of bilingualism.
narrative assessments should be conducted in both languages for bilingual children.
